# CMS Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 8: SNF coverage

- Citation: CMS, Medicare Benefit Policy Manual, Chapter 8, "Coverage of Extended Care (SNF) Services Under Hospital Insurance". https://www.cms.gov/regulations-and-guidance/guidance/manuals/downloads/bp102c08pdf.pdf (PDF read locally, about 22,000 words; PDF not committed)
- Tier: 1
- Applies to MA: yes, for SNF coverage criteria, per CMS-4201-F (`cms-2023-ma-coverage-criteria-rule.md`) and the Jimmo settlement (applies to MA as well, per the CMS fact sheet and the Center for Medicare Advocacy).
- Key passages:
  - §30, four-factor test: SNF care is covered if all are met: (1) the patient requires skilled nursing or skilled rehabilitation services; (2) "on a daily basis"; (3) "as a practical matter … can be provided only on an inpatient basis in a SNF"; (4) the services are "reasonable and necessary". "If any one of these four factors is not met, a stay … is not covered."
  - §30 and §30.2 (Jimmo): "Coverage of nursing care and/or therapy to perform a maintenance program does not turn on the presence or absence of an individual's potential for improvement … but rather on the beneficiary's need for skilled care." Skilled nursing is covered when needed "to maintain the patient's current condition or prevent or slow further deterioration".
  - §30.6, daily: skilled nursing on "essentially a 7-days-a-week basis", or skilled rehab "at least 5 days a week". The requirement "should not be applied so strictly that it would not be met merely because there is an isolated break of a day or two".
  - §30.2.3.1-30.2.3.3: management and evaluation of a care plan, observation and assessment, and teaching and training can themselves be skilled services (not read in detail).
  - §20.1-20.2: 3-day prior hospitalization; 30-day transfer rule (MA plans may waive the 3-day rule; *background*, not verified).
- Limits: manual guidance, not statute; how MA plans apply it, and how CMS enforces it, were not researched.
- Relevance: a structured, public rulebook against which a payer's stated denial reason can be checked. Common contestable reasons map to specific sections: "not improving" or "plateaued" (Jimmo, §30), "missed therapy days" (§30.6), "custodial only" (§30.2.3). ExaCare's Managed Care Agent already uses "CMS Chapter 8 Guidelines" for out-of-network and PDPM authorizations (`kb/4-submit-preauth.md`, `kb/3-manage-payer.md`).
